ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
register_map_kind: Two-layer register architecture: DP layer (Debug Port, accessed directly via SWD transactions with APnDP=0) + AP layer (Access Port, accessed with APnDP=1; up to 256 APs selected via SELECT.APSEL[7:0], each exposing a 64-byte register window banked via SELECT.APBANKSEL[7:4]).
base_address: DP registers are at addresses 0x0/0x4/0x8/0xC (A[2:3] encoded into the Request packet); each AP exposes 64 bytes (16 registers) at offsets 0x00..0x3C via A[2:3] + APBANKSEL banking; AP IDR is at fixed offset 0xFC, BASE at 0xF8.

registers.name: ABORT
registers.purpose: Aborts an in-flight AP transaction and clears sticky error bits in CTRL/STAT.

field_map.name: DAPABORT
field_map.description: Generate a DAP abort (cancel any in-flight AP transaction).

registers.name: IDCODE/DPIDR
registers.purpose: Identifies the Debug Port designer + version + revision. Always the host's first transaction after power-up or line reset.

field_map.name: REVISION
field_map.description: Revision number of the DP design (designer-defined).

field_map.name: MIN
field_map.description: Minimum DP version supported (0 = ADIv5; 1 = ADIv5.1+).

field_map.name: VERSION
field_map.description: DP architecture version (0 = DPv0/JTAG-DP only; 1 = DPv1/SW-DP basic; 2 = DPv2/ADIv5.1+; 3 = DPv3/ADIv5.2 multi-drop).

field_map.name: DESIGNER
field_map.description: JEP106 manufacturer ID of the DP designer (11 bits = 7-bit JEP106 + 4-bit JEP106 continuation count).

field_map.name: RAO
field_map.description: Read-As-One — hard-wired to 1 so that the DP IDCODE is distinguishable from a stuck-at-zero bus.

registers.name: CTRL/STAT
registers.purpose: Read: sticky error status and power-up acknowledge. Write: request system / debug power-up + reset + turnaround count.

field_map.name: STICKYORUN
field_map.description: Sticky overrun bit — set when a posted read overruns (RW1C via ABORT.ORUNERRCLR).

field_map.name: TRNCNT
field_map.description: Turnaround SWCLK cycle count (00=1 cycle; 11=4 cycles).

field_map.name: MASKLANE
field_map.description: Per-byte mask lanes for compare-against-DLPIDR feature.

field_map.name: WDATAERR
field_map.description: Write Data Error sticky bit — set on Data Parity mismatch during a write (RW1C via ABORT.WDERRCLR).

field_map.name: READOK
field_map.description: Read-OK status — set when a previous DP read succeeded.

field_map.name: STICKYERR
field_map.description: Sticky AP transfer error (RW1C via ABORT.STKERRCLR).

field_map.name: STICKYCMP
field_map.description: Sticky compare-match bit (used with DLPIDR for multi-drop) (RW1C via ABORT.STKCMPCLR).

field_map.name: CDBGRSTREQ
field_map.description: Debug reset request (host writes 1; target acks via CDBGRSTACK).

registers.name: SELECT
registers.purpose: Banks the AP layer + DP higher-bank registers.

field_map.name: DPBANKSEL
field_map.description: DP bank select (bank 0 = CTRL/STAT, bank 2 = TARGETID, bank 3 = DLPIDR, bank 4 = EVENTSTAT).

field_map.name: APBANKSEL
field_map.description: AP bank select — high 4 bits of the AP register offset (A[3:2] are encoded into the Request packet).

registers.name: RDBUFF
registers.purpose: Returns the data of the most recent posted AP read. Reading RDBUFF flushes the posted-read queue and is the canonical way to recover the final read of a burst.

registers.name: TARGETID
registers.purpose: Identifies the target SoC (not the DP itself). Used by hosts to confirm they are talking to the expected SoC.

registers.name: DLPIDR
registers.long_name: DP Data Link Protocol Identification Register
registers.purpose: Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2): identifies this specific target instance on a shared SWDIO/SWCLK bus.

field_map.name: TINSTANCE
field_map.description: Target instance number (0..15 if 16 targets share a bus).

registers.name: EVENTSTAT
registers.purpose: Per-target event status (e.g. CPU halted, watchpoint matched). Bits are vendor-defined.

field_map.name: AddrInc
field_map.description: Auto-increment mode: 00=Off, 01=Single (increment by transfer size), 10=Packed (multiple sub-word transfers per DRW), 11=Reserved.

field_map.name: Prot
field_map.description: Protection bits — AHB HPROT[6:0] or AXI ARPROT[2:0] depending on bus type.

registers.name: TAR
registers.purpose: The 32-bit (or 64-bit) system-bus address used by the next DRW transfer. Auto-incremented per CSW.AddrInc after each DRW read/write.

registers.name: DRW
registers.purpose: Data conduit: a write of DRW pushes the 32-bit value to system-bus address TAR; a read of DRW returns the value at TAR (posted — actual value via the next RDBUFF or next read). TAR auto-increments per CSW.AddrInc.

registers.name: BASE
registers.long_name: MEM-AP Debug Component ROM Table Base Register
registers.purpose: Points to the 4 KB CoreSight ROM Table that enumerates this AP's debug components.

field_map.name: Present
field_map.description: 1 = ROM Table is present at the indicated address.

field_map.name: BASEADDR
field_map.description: Bits[31:12] of the ROM Table address.

registers.name: IDR
registers.purpose: Identifies the AP type and designer.

field_map.name: Type
field_map.description: AP type code: 0=JTAG-AP, 1=AMBA AHB3-AP, 2=AMBA APB2/3-AP, 4=AMBA AXI3/4-AP, 5=AMBA AHB5-AP, 8=AMBA APB4/5-AP.

selection_rule: DP registers are at A[3:2] = 0x0 / 0x4 / 0x8 / 0xC selected via APnDP=0 in the Request. Higher-bank DP registers (TARGETID/DLPIDR/EVENTSTAT) are reached by writing SELECT.DPBANKSEL first. AP registers are at A[3:2] = 0x0 / 0x4 / 0x8 / 0xC selected via APnDP=1; the high 4 bits of the AP register offset come from SELECT.APBANKSEL; the AP index comes from SELECT.APSEL. AP IDR (0xFC) and BASE (0xF8) are at fixed high banks.

ap_class_codes_table.0x0: JTAG-AP — forwards transactions to a downstream JTAG TAP

notes: The DP and AP layers are orthogonal in addressing: APnDP=0 selects DP (4 registers per bank); APnDP=1 selects AP (16 registers per AP × 256 APs). DP addresses are not memory-mapped per se — they are encoded by A[3:2] bits in the 8-bit Request. AP addresses are encoded by SELECT.APSEL + APBANKSEL + A[3:2]. The MEM-AP variant adds an in-AP 32/64-bit TAR + DRW pair that maps to a wide system-bus address space (typically the entire SoC's debug bus reachable via AHB/APB/AXI).
